title: CmdPal: Some UI messages handled by MainWindow are not marshaled to the dispatcher thread

judgment.rationale: The report identifies a concrete UI-thread consistency defect and current code shows mixed dispatcher handling, but exact sender/order constraints remain to be confirmed.
evidence: Issue is assigned to a Command Palette maintainer and targets MainWindow message handling.
MainWindow.xaml.cs contains multiple message receivers and UI/HWND mutations.
Program activation redirection requires preserving synchronous completion.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the dispatcher-boundary design after collecting the affected-message sender/thread trace.

fix_assessment.rationale: A repository change is applicable, but the exact dispatcher and completion strategy needs a focused trace.

proposed_fixes.title: Make MainWindow messenger UI mutations consistently dispatcher-bound
proposed_fixes.root_cause: MainWindow receives messages that can originate outside the UI thread, but the current receiver implementations do not apply one consistent UI/HWND affinity rule.
plan: Inventory every MainWindow IRecipient<T>.Receive implementation and classify UI, HWND, and shared-state mutations.
Move UI-affine work behind private dispatcher-thread handlers while preserving synchronous activation completion.
Add focused tests or seams for message dispatch and manually exercise summon, dock, dismiss, drag, and quit flows.
verification: Build the Command Palette UI project in the supported Visual Studio configuration.
Deliver affected messages from a non-UI sender and verify UI/HWND access occurs on MainWindow.DispatcherQueue.
Redirect a second-instance activation and verify the payload is processed once before the sender exits.

confidence.rationale: The mixed receiver implementations are visible in current code, but sender-thread and ordering constraints need confirmation.

issue_context.summary: A Command Palette maintainer reports that MainWindow handles related UI/window messages inconsistently: some receivers marshal to the dispatcher while others touch window state directly.
known_information: Issue is on main and is assigned to a Command Palette maintainer.
The report specifically concerns UI/window messages handled by MainWindow.
Current MainWindow.xaml.cs contains multiple IRecipient<T>.Receive implementations and mixed dispatcher usage.
Program activation redirection has a synchronous completion path that must be preserved.
inferences: Some direct receivers may run from a non-UI messenger sender, but the issue does not identify every sender thread.
A blanket asynchronous dispatch could change activation or dismissal ordering.
issue_context.analysis: The code evidence supports a focused dispatcher-boundary design, but the exact safe change depends on sender-thread and synchronous-ordering facts.
initial_investigation: MainWindow.xaml.cs is the owning file for messenger receivers, HWND access, and show/hide state.
Program.cs and App.xaml.cs establish redirected activation and initial window creation constraints.
The prior duplicate/issue search found no stronger duplicate; this is a targeted implementation-quality bug.

information_gaps.information: Thread and ordering behavior for each affected message receiver.
information_gaps.why_needed: Distinguishes safe TryEnqueue changes from changes that require a completion mechanism.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Run a dev build with message names and managed/native thread IDs logged at send and receive.

actions.label: Request CmdPal message-thread trace
actions.note: Confirm the sender and ordering constraints before changing dispatcher behavior.

comment.body: The report identifies a real consistency problem: some MainWindow UI/window messages are dispatcher-marshaled while others are handled directly. Please provide a short trace or code-level confirmation for the affected messages (for example ShowWindowMessage, ShowPaletteAtMessage, HideWindowMessage, QuitMessage, and DismissMessage): which thread sends each message, and whether the sender requires synchronous completion before returning. This evidence determines whether each receiver can safely enqueue work or needs a completion signal; it can be collected from a local dev build with thread IDs and the existing messenger logging.

actions.label: Design fix: marshal CmdPal window messages
actions.note: Approve a fork-side design after confirming the sender/thread ordering constraints.
actions.design_prompt: Inspect MainWindow messenger receivers and make UI/HWND mutations consistently dispatcher-bound without breaking synchronous activation completion.

design.root_cause: MainWindow receives messages that can originate outside the UI thread, but the current receiver implementations do not apply one consistent UI/HWND affinity rule.
evidence: Current MainWindow.xaml.cs contains messenger receivers for show, hide, dismiss, quit, dock, and related UI state.
Existing dispatcher-bound receivers demonstrate that UI affinity is already an established pattern in this component.
Program.OnActivated/RedirectActivationTo impose a synchronous activation contract.

affected_files.purpose: Owns Command Palette window state, messenger registration, show/hide behavior, and HWND access.
Redirects activation to an existing instance and defines synchronous completion behavior.
Creates MainWindow and hands initial activation to it.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Receivers mix direct UI/HWND operations with dispatcher-enqueued work.
implementation_steps.change: Classify each receiver by thread affinity and extract UI-only private handlers; receivers should enqueue only work that is safe to defer.
implementation_steps.code_block: foreach (receiver in MainWindowReceivers) { classify(receiver); receiver => DispatcherQueue.TryEnqueue(() => HandleOnUiThread(receiver)); }
edge_cases: Do not defer state whose sender requires synchronous acknowledgement.
Preserve existing message ordering for show/dismiss/quit.
tests: Add dispatcher-boundary tests for each affected message.
Verify HWND operations run only on the UI thread.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Redirected activation depends on the target instance completing message handling before the source exits.
implementation_steps.change: Keep the synchronous contract; use an explicit completion signal if dispatch becomes asynchronous.
implementation_steps.code_block: var completion = new TaskCompletionSource(); messenger.Send(message); await completion.Task; return;
edge_cases: Handle a closed target window and cancellation.
tests: Exercise second-instance activation and payload delivery exactly once.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Initial launch creates the window on the UI thread and begins activation handling.
implementation_steps.change: Verify the same dispatcher policy applies to initial and redirected activation paths.
tests: Launch normally and through a redirected activation.

verify: Build the Command Palette UI project.
Run dispatcher-boundary tests or a dev diagnostic build.
Manually summon, dock, drag, dismiss, quit, and repeat the sequence.
risks: Changing dispatch timing can affect focus, visibility, and shutdown ordering.
Incorrect completion handling could lose redirected activation payloads or deadlock startup.
alternatives: Leaving direct receivers unchanged is unsafe for UI/HWND access from worker threads.
Making every receiver fire-and-forget is rejected because activation has a synchronous contract.
